results.content: US wholesale inflation shot higher in September, soaring to its highest level in more than four years, Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed Thursday. The Producer Price Index rose 1.3% from August and 6.3% from the year before, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data. Economists were expecting PPI to increase 0.5% from August and 5.3% annually, according to FactSet. It’s the fastest monthly increase since March 2022 and the highest annual rate since December 2022, the year when US inflation hit a 40-year high.
